Venezuelan Technology Services Workers Launch Nationwide Walkout, Halting Projects

CARACAS, June 17—Thousands of workers in Venezuela’s technology services industry walked off the job Monday, disrupting operations at dozens of key firms across the country and putting critical software development and IT consulting projects on hold.

The strike, called by the National Union of Technology Professionals (UNIPROT), began in the early hours of the morning after negotiations with employers over wage increases and improved working conditions broke down over the weekend. The union said that more than 80 percent of its 12,000 members were participating, affecting firms specializing in cloud computing, cybersecurity, and enterprise software solutions.

Major technology services firms including DataSoluciones, Innovatech Venezuela, and RedPixel reported near-total shutdowns at their main offices in Caracas, Maracaibo, and Valencia. “We’ve had to suspend all client-facing IT support and ongoing software rollouts as our engineers and consultants are not reporting to work,” said Sofia Benítez, spokesperson for DataSoluciones.

Industry executives warned that if the strike continues, it could set back the delivery of key projects for local clients. “We are deeply concerned about the impact on our workforce and project timelines,” said Daniel Morales, CEO of Innovatech Venezuela. “We urge all parties to return to the negotiating table.”

UNIPROT said workers are demanding a 60 percent wage increase and better healthcare benefits. “Our members are vital to the country’s digital infrastructure, but they are struggling to make ends meet,” said union leader Armando Figueroa. He added that the strike would continue until “meaningful offers” are made.

The Venezuelan Technology Services Chamber said it was seeking mediation to resolve the dispute. Talks have not yet been scheduled as of Monday afternoon.
